questions.text: Define the following terms with reference to the relational data model: (i) relation schema, (ii) degree of a relation, (iii) domain of an attribute, (iv) superkey. State the entity integrity constraint and the referential integrity constraint.

Consider the following schema:
Student(student_id, name, dept_code, cgpa)
Department(dept_code, dept_name, hod_name)
With reference to the above schema, explain the difference between a candidate key, a primary key and a foreign key. Describe what happens to the tuples of Student when a Department tuple is deleted under the ON DELETE CASCADE option and under the ON DELETE SET NULL option.

A private university wishes to computerise its course registration process. A student is identified by a student id and has a name and a department. A course has a course code, a title and credit hours. A course is offered as one or more sections in a semester, and every section is taught by exactly one teacher. A student may register for many sections and a section may have many students registered in it.
Draw an ER diagram for the above scenario. Show all entity sets, relationship sets, primary key attributes, and the cardinality and participation constraints.
Convert the ER diagram of Question 2(a) into a set of relations. For each relation, underline the primary key and clearly indicate the foreign keys, if any.

Consider the following schema:
Book(isbn, title, author, price, publisher_id)
Publisher(publisher_id, pname, city)
Sales(isbn, branch_code, quantity)
(i) Write a relational algebra expression to find the titles of the books published by publishers located in 'Dhaka'.
(ii) Write an SQL query to list the name of each publisher along with the total quantity of books sold by that publisher.
(iii) Write an SQL query to find the titles of the books that have never been sold.

Consider the relation
Project(emp_id, emp_name, project_id, project_name, hours_worked, dept_name, dept_head)
with the following functional dependencies:
emp_id -> emp_name, dept_name
dept_name -> dept_head
project_id -> project_name
emp_id, project_id -> hours_worked
(i) Identify the candidate key of the relation and justify your answer.
(ii) Identify the insertion, deletion and update anomalies present in the relation.
(iii) Decompose the relation up to 3NF, showing the relations obtained at each step.
Explain the ACID properties of a transaction. For each property, describe one situation in a banking application in which a violation of that property would leave the database in an incorrect state.
What is a schedule? List the states through which a transaction passes during its execution and name the two types of failure that a recovery manager must handle.
